Teodosić''' ({{lang-sr-cyr|Милош Теодосић}}, born March 19, 1987) is a Serbian sports director and former professional [[basketball]] player. He also represented the [[Serbia men's national basketball team|National Basketball Team of Serbia]] internationally. He primarily played the [[point guard]] and [[shooting guard]] positions. He is a six time [[All-EuroLeague]] selection, and was voted [[EuroLeague MVP]] in [[Euroleague 2009–10|2010]].{{cite web | url = https://www.fiba.basketball/basketballworldcup/2014/player/Milos-Teodosic | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20140804005908/http://www.fiba.com/basketballworldcup/2014/Milos-TEODOSIC | url-status = live | archive-date = August 4, 2014 | title = TEODOSIĆ, Miloš | publisher = FIBA.com | access-date = August 18, 2015}}{{cite web | url = http://www.euroleague.net/competition/players/showplayer?pcode=JDR | title = TEODOSIĆ, Miloš | publisher = EUROLEAGUE.net | access-date = August 18, 2015}} Under Teodosić the Serbia national team won a [[EuroBasket]] silver medal in [[EuroBasket 2009|2009]], as well as a [[FIBA Basketball World Cup]] silver medal in [[2014 FIBA Basketball World Cup|2014]], being elected to the All-Tournament Team in both competitions. He also won an Olympic silver medal at the [[Basketball at the 2016 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2016 Rio Games]].{{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20160819122714/http://archive.fiba.com/pages/eng/fa/p/rpp/150/q/Milos%20TEODOSIC/pid/44167/_//players.html|title=FIBA.com profile}} He was named [[FIBA Europe Men's Player of the Year Award|FIBA Europe Player of the Year]] in 2010, and in 2016, he was voted the best non-NBA player in the world by NBA coaches,{{Cite news|url=http://www.opencourt-basketball.com/milos-teodosic-the-best-non-nba-player-in-the-world/|title=Milos Teodosic – The Best Non NBA Player in the World|last=Peters|first=Damien|date=October 24, 2016|newspaper=Opencourt Basketball|access-date=November 22, 2016}} as well as the [[Euroscar|European Player of the Year]] by ''[[La Gazzetta dello Sport]]''.{{cite news|url=http://www.gazzetta.it/Basket/16-01-2017/basket-euro-player-2016-teodosic-nba-battuta-16-anni-180435253039.shtml |title=Basket, Euro Player 2016 a Teodosic: Nba battuta dopo 16 anni | newspaper=La Gazzetta dello Sport |date=January 16, 2017 |access-date=January 16, 2017|language=it}} ==Professional career== Following his retirement as an active player, Teodosić transitioned into executive roles, serving as a sports director. ===Early years=== He began playing basketball in hometown clubs KK Student and [[KK Metalac Valjevo|Metalac]]. He then moved to Belgrade-based club [[KK FMP (1991–2011)|FMP]] where he signed his first professional contract. After being loaned to [[KK Borac Čačak|Borac Čačak]] for the 2005–06 season, he had a breakthrough 2006–07 season. Over 16 games in the [[2006–07 ULEB Cup|ULEB Cup]] (now called [[EuroCup Basketball|EuroCup]]), he averaged 7.8 points, 2.9 assists, and 2.1 rebounds per game. FMP was eventually eliminated in the semi-final of this [[European professional club basketball system|second-tier level]] European-wide competition.{{cite news|title=Pirova pobeda FMP-a u Železniku|url=http://www.pressonline.rs/sport/ostali-sportovi/6736/pirova-pobeda-fmp-a-u-zelezniku.html|access-date=September 15, 2014|work=pressonline.rs|language=sr}} They also played in the final series of the [[2006–07 ABA NLB League|Adriatic League]] playoffs, where they lost to [[KK Partizan|Partizan Belgrade]]. ===Olympiacos (2007–2011)=== [[File:Petar Božić (cropped).jpg|thumb|left|180px|Teodosić in 2009]] In 2007, Teodosić signed a five-year contract with [[Olympiacos B.C.|Olympiacos]] of the [[Greek Basket League]], worth €2.8 million [[net income]] (after taxes). Olympiacos also had to pay a buyout to FMP, to secure his rights. The contract he signed with Olympiacos included a €1.3 million buyout clause amount. However, the contract also stipulated that Olympiacos would hold the right to match any offer made to him by another club that offered to pay his buyout.[http://www.redplanet.gr/basket/o-teontosits-kai-to-symvolaio-toy.1100813.html Redplanet.gr Ο Τεόντοσιτς και το συμβόλαιο του {{in lang|el}}.] In the [[2009–10 Euroleague]] season, Teodosić averaged 13.4 [[point (basketball)|points]], 2.5 [[rebound (basketball)|rebounds]], 4.9 [[assist (basketball)|assists]], and 1.8 [[steal (basketball)|steals]] per game, all career highs up to that point. Teodosić played a crucial role in [[Olympiacos B.C.|Olympiacos Pireaus]], reaching the [[EuroLeague Final Four]], where they eventually lost [[2010 Euroleague Final Four|in the final]] to [[FC Barcelona Bàsquet|FC Barcelona]], after beating [[KK Partizan]] in the semi-final. Teodosić was voted onto the [[All-EuroLeague Team|All-EuroLeague First Team]], and on May 8, 2010, he was officially announced as the [[EuroLeague MVP|EuroLeague 2010 MVP]], his first, and to this date only, EuroLeague MVP award win in his career. ===CSKA Moscow (2011–2017)=== On July 6, 2011, Teodosić signed a three-year contract with [[PBC CSKA Moscow|CSKA Moscow]] of the [[Russian Professional Basketball League|Russian League]] and [[VTB United League]].[http://www.euroleague.net/euroleaguenews/transactions/2011-12-signings/i/86497/5611/cska-moscow-lands-teodosic CSKA MOSCOW lands Teodosic.][http://www.cskabasket.com/news/?a=news&id=9943&lang=en Milos Teodosic moved to CSKA.] The contract was worth [[euro sign|€]]5.7 million euros [[net income]].[http://www.redplanet.gr/basket/anakoinwthhke-epishma-apo-thn-tsska-o-teontosits.1176507.html Redplanet.gr Ανακοινώθηκε επίσημα από την ΤΣΣΚΑ ο Τεόντοσιτς {{in lang|el}}.] In his first season with the Russian club, he led them to the [[EuroLeague Final]], where they lost 62–61 to his former club, [[Olympiacos B.C.|Olympiacos]]. He was named to the [[All-EuroLeague]] Second Team before the start of the [[2011 Euroleague Final Four|Final Four]].{{cite web|title=Kirilenko, Krstic and Teodosic are the 2011–12 All-Euroleague team nominees|url=http://www.cskabasket.com/news/?id=11079&lang=en%7Cwork=cskabasket.com|work=cskabasket.com|access-date=May 18, 2012}} His second season with CSKA was statistically even better for him, as he averaged 12.7 points, 4.9 assists, and a career-high 2.8 rebounds in the EuroLeague. He was also once again named to the [[All-EuroLeague]] Second Team, his second consecutive nomination.{{cite web|title=2012–13 All-Euroleague First and Second Teams announced|url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/113030/180|website=euroleague.net|access-date=July 1, 2014}} ;2013–14 season After beating [[Panathinaikos B.C.|Panathinaikos]] in the quarterfinal playoff series round in the [[2013–14 Euroleague]], CSKA Moscow lost in the semi-final of the [[2013–14 Euroleague Final Four|EuroLeague Final Four]] to [[Maccabi Tel Aviv B.C.|Maccabi Tel Aviv]].{{cite web|title=Maccabi rallies from 15 down to stun CSKA, advance to championship game!|url=http://www.euroleague.net/main/results/showgame?gamecode=251&seasoncode=E2013#!report|work=Euroleague.net|access-date=May 20, 2014}} Shortly after failing to win the EuroLeague for the third straight year, the president of CSKA blamed Teodosić and his Serbian teammate, [[Nenad Krstić]], for not putting enough effort in over the season.{{cite web|title=Predsednik CSKA više neće Tea i Krleta|url=http://www.24sata.rs/sport/vesti/vest/predsednik-cska-vise-nece-tea-i-krleta/136699.phtml|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140521045651/http://www.24sata.rs/sport/vesti/vest/predsednik-cska-vise-nece-tea-i-krleta/136699.phtml|url-status=usurped|archive-date=May 21, 2014|work=24sata.rs|access-date=May 20, 2014|language=sr}}{{cite web|title=Teodosić: Sami smo krivi|url=http://www.b92.net/sport/vesti.php?yyyy=2014&mm=05&dd=17&nav_id=849235|work=b92.net|access-date=May 20, 2014|language=sr}} Back on the Russian national domestic league front, shortly after the EuroLeague Final Four, CSKA was facing elimination in the [[2013–14 VTB United League|VTB United League]] playoff quarterfinal series versus [[PBC Lokomotiv-Kuban|Lokomotiv Kuban]], trailing 0–2, without home court advantage. Teodosić and Krstić helped CSKA storm back to win the series 3–2, after the large deficit, to advance to the league's semi-finals, as they answered the previous criticism from the club's president. Eventually, CSKA won the VTB United League by sweeping [[BC Nizhny Novgorod|Nizhny Novgorod]] 3–0 in the finals series.{{cite web|title=CSKA crowned champions!!!|url=http://www.vtb-league.com/en/news/cska-crowned-champions.htm|website=vtb-league.com|access-date=June 14, 2014|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140617172025/http://www.vtb-league.com/en/news/cska-crowned-champions.htm|archive-date=June 17, 2014}} Teodosić was named the [[VTB United League Playoffs MVP|VTB Playoffs MVP]]. Despite winning the VTB United League, the 2013–14 season was seen as a disappointment for CSKA, and it was expected that Teodosić, as well as his teammate [[Nenad Krstić]], and team [[head coach]] [[Ettore Messina]], could all leave the club over the summer.{{cite web|title=Teodosic, Krstic and Messina likely to leave CSKA Moscow|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/russia/119931/teodosic-krstic-and-messina-likely-to-leave-cska-moscow.html|website=sportando.net|access-date=July 1, 2014}} Eventually, Krstić and Messina left the club. However, in June 2014, Teodosić extended his contract with the club for three more years.{{cite web|title=CSKA Moscow officially extends Milos Teodosic for three years|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/russia/124930/cska-moscow-officially-extends-milos-teodosic-for-three-years.html|website=sportando.net|access-date=July 1, 2014}} ;2014–15 season On November 7, 2014, in a [[2014–15 Euroleague|EuroLeague]] game victory against [[Baloncesto Málaga|Unicaja Málaga]], Teodosić recorded a career-high 27 points, while also adding 10 assists.{{cite news|title=Teodosic stars as CSKA downs Unicaja in battle of unbeatens|url=http://www.euroleague.net/main/results/showgame?gamecode=41&pcode=JDR&seasoncode=E2014#!report|access-date=November 8, 2014|work=euroleague.net}} In May 2015, he was named to the [[All-EuroLeague Team|All-EuroLeague First Team]] for his performances throughout the season.{{cite news|title=All-Euroleague First and Second Teams announced|url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/5xtj7vjfuokfw7g8|access-date=May 8, 2015|work=euroleague.net}} CSKA Moscow managed to advance to the [[2015 Euroleague Final Four|EuroLeague Final Four]] for the fourth straight season, after eliminating [[Panathinaikos B.C.|Panathinaikos]], for the second straight season in the [[2014–15 Euroleague Quarter-finals|quarter-finals]] series 3–1.{{cite news|title=CSKA Moscow routs Panathinaikos to claim Final Four berth|url=http://www.euroleague.net/main/results/showgame?gamecode=246&seasoncode=E2014#!report|access-date=May 18, 2015|work=euroleague.net|date=April 22, 2015}} However, in the semi-final game, despite being dubbed by media members as the favorite to advance, CSKA Moscow once again lost to [[Olympiacos B.C.|Olympiacos]]. The final score was 70–68, after Olympiacos came back in the 4th quarter, led by [[Vassilis Spanoulis]].{{cite news|title=Spanoulis comes through again as Olympiacos stuns CSKA|url=http://www.euroleague.net/main/results/showgame?gamecode=249&seasoncode=E2014#!report|access-date=May 18, 2015|work=euroleague.net|date=May 15, 2015}} Teodosić was ineffective in the game, scoring 8 points, on 2 for 9 shooting, with 5 assists, and 6 turnovers. CSKA Moscow eventually finished in third place, after defeating [[Fenerbahçe Men's Basketball|Fenerbahçe]] 86–80 in the third place game,{{cite news|title=CSKA Moscow beats Fenerbahce in third-place game|url=http://www.euroleague.net/main/results/showgame?gamecode=250&seasoncode=E2014#!report|access-date=May 18, 2015|work=eurolague.net|date=May 17, 2015}} in a game which Teodosić did not play, due to muscle fatigue.{{cite news|title=Teodosic se borra. ¿Por qué no jugó hoy?|url=http://planetadeporte.es/baloncesto/euroleague/2015/17051857-769452|access-date=May 18, 2015|work=planetadeporte.es|date=May 17, 2015|language=es}} Teodosić, however, had one of his best seasons in his time at the club, averaging a career-high 14.8 points, 2.8 rebounds, and a league-leading 7 assists, over 24 games played in the EuroLeague. CSKA Moscow finished the season by winning the [[2014–15 VTB United League|VTB United League]], after eliminating [[BC Khimki|Khimki]] 3–0 in the league's finals series.{{cite news|title=CSKA wins championship! |url=http://www.vtb-league.com/en/news/cska-wins-championship.htm |access-date=June 10, 2015 |work=vtb-league.com |date=June 8, 2015 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150610135415/http://www.vtb-league.com/en/news/cska-wins-championship.htm |archive-date=June 10, 2015 }} ;2015–16 season [[File:JSF Nanterre - CSKA Moscou, Euroligue, 17 October 2013 - 16.JPG|thumb|left|220px|Teodosić with [[CSKA Moscow]] during the warm-up]] In the 2015–16 EuroLeague season, Teodosić formed one of the deadliest 1–2 punches in the EuroLeague, along with [[Nando de Colo]], who ended up being voted the season's [[EuroLeague MVP]]. The team solidified its quality with the usual good results prior to the EuroLeague Final Four, with Teodosić playing one of the best seasons of his career. He shot the ball very efficiently overall in each stage of the competition. The year proved to be successful for CSKA, as they finally won the EuroLeague championship, after beating [[Fenerbahçe Men's Basketball|Fenerbahce Ulker Istanbul]] 101–96 [[2016 Euroleague Final Four|in the finals]], after [[overtime (sports)|overtime]]. Individually, Teodosić was a key player in the win, posting 19 points, 7 assists, 5 rebounds, and 2 steals, and thus, finally winning the EuroLeague title, after several previous failed attempts to do so in the EuroLeague Final Four. ;2016–17 season On October 31, 2016, he was named the October 2016 [[EuroLeague MVP of the Month]].{{cite news|title=Turkish Airlines EuroLeague MVP for October: Milos Teodosic of CSKA Moscow|url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/7dh9kswi7oeb6o78|access-date=November 4, 2016|work=euroleague.net|date=October 31, 2016}} His [[performance index rating]] of 43 in the Round 9 was the highest in the EuroLeague that season and the second-best in CSKA's illustrious history.{{cite web|url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/7fjuruc75mn78iac/regular-season-round-9-mvp-milos-teodosic-cska-moscow|title=Regular Season, Round 9 MVP: Milos Teodosic, CSKA Moscow|publisher=EuroLeague|date=November 26, 2016}} CSKA Moscow finished the season winning the 3rd place at the [[2017 EuroLeague Final Four]] and winning the [[2016–17 VTB United League|VTB United League]]. Teodosić averaged career-high-tying 16.1 points and season-best 6.8 assists over 29 EuroLeague games. At the end of the season his contract with CSKA Moscow expired and he left the club.{{cite news|title=Thank you, Milos!|url=http://www.cskabasket.com/news/?id=16188&lang=en|access-date=July 7, 2017|work=cskabasket.com|date=July 7, 2017}} ===Los Angeles Clippers (2017–2019)=== On July 10, 2017, Teodosić signed a two-year, $12.3 million contract with the [[Los Angeles Clippers]], with the second year being a player option.{{cite press release |title=LA Clippers sign Serbian guard Milos Teodosic |url=https://www.nba.com/news/la-clippers-sign-guard-milos-teodosic |publisher=NBA |access-date=26 February 2022 |date=11 July 2017}} During the NBA pre-season games, Teodosić showed potential as an above-average passer in the NBA.{{cite news|last1=Xypteras|first1=Tony|title=Milos Teodosic Proved He's The World's Best Passer in His NBA Debut with the Clippers|url=https://uproxx.com/dimemag/milos-teodosic-nba-debut-clippers/|access-date=December 24, 2019|work=uproxx.com|date=October 2, 2017}}{{cite news|last1=Barnewall|first1=Chris|title=Clippers point guard Milos Teodosic is a name every basketball fan needs to know|url=https://www.cbssports.com/nba/news/clippers-point-guard-milos-teodosic-is-a-name-every-basketball-fan-needs-to-know|access-date=October 24, 2017|work=cbssports.com|date=October 13, 2017}} On October 19, 2017, Teodosić made his NBA debut against the [[Los Angeles Lakers]], recording 6 points and 6 assists. In the second game of 2017–18 season against the [[Phoenix Suns]], Teodosić suffered a [[Plantar fasciitis|plantar fascia injury]] in his left foot and was put out indefinitely due to the unpredictability of the recovery time for such injury.{{cite news|title=Injury Report: Milos Teodosic|url=http://www.nba.com/clippers/injury-report-milos-teodosic/|access-date=October 24, 2017|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=October 22, 2017}} On December 11, he returned on the court after 22 games of absence, against the [[Toronto Raptors]], scoring 12 points and grabbing 7 rebounds in a 96–91 home victory.{{cite news|last1=Woike|first1=Dan|title=Clippers get Milos Teodosic back, but Danilo Gallinari again is sidelined with glute injury|url=http://www.latimes.com/sports/clippers/la-sp-clippers-report-20171211-story.html|access-date=December 12, 2017|work=Los Angeles Times|date=December 11, 2017}} In his first NBA season, battling with persistent plantar fasciitis injury, he averaged 9.5 points, 4.6 assists and 2.8 rebounds over 45 games, while shooting 41.9% from the field. On June 24, 2018, he exercised his player option with the Clippers for the 2018–19 season.{{cite news |last1=Flom |first1=Robert |title=Milos Teodosic Exercises Player Option for the 2018–19 Season |url=https://www.clipsnation.com/2018/6/24/17498814/milos-teodosic-exercises-player-option-for-2018-2019-season-clippers |access-date=June 24, 2018 |work=clipsnation.com |date=June 24, 2018}} On February 7, 2019, he was waived by the Clippers.{{cite web |title=L.A. On June 26, 2025, Teodosić announced his retirement from basketball.{{cite web|title=Milos Teodosic retires at 38: “Immense THANKS to everyone” |url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/euroleague/1841779/milos-teodosic-retires-euroleague-nba/|website=eurohoops.net|date=June 26, 2025|access-date=June 26, 2025}} ==National team career== {{see also|2016 Serbia men's Olympic basketball team}} [[File:Teodosićs game-winning 3-pointer over Garbajosa.jpg|thumb|220px|Teodosić's game-winning [[Three-point field goal|3-pointer]] over [[Jorge Garbajosa]] during the [[2010 FIBA World Championship]] quarterfinal versus [[Spain men's national basketball team|Spain]].]] Teodosić was a member of the Serbian junior national teams. Playing with Serbia's junior national teams, he won the gold medal at the [[2003 FIBA Europe Under-16 Championship|2003]] [[FIBA Europe Under-16 Championship]]. He also won the gold medal at the [[2005 FIBA Europe Under-18 Championship]]. He was named the [[Most valuable player|MVP]] of the [[2007 FIBA Europe Under-20 Championship|2007]] [[FIBA Europe Under-20 Championship]],[http://www.fibaeurope.com/cid_KNce8jInH7Qj1EsyH5rjn2.teamID_96799.compID_UIfgjyQcGqk-fPlnl66Tj0.season_2007.roundID_5499.coid_axrH56pLHQ-nigMnn6aUU3.articleMode_on.html FIBAEurope.com MVP Award: Teodosic Tops The Polls.] where he also won the gold medal. He currently plays for the [[Serbia men's national basketball team|Serbia national basketball]] senior team. With the senior men's Serbia national team, he played at the [[EuroBasket 2007]]. At the [[EuroBasket 2009]], he reached the final with Serbia, and was named to the All-Tournament Team. In 2010, Teodosić was named to the Serbian roster for the [[2010 FIBA World Championship]]. After being suspended for a brawl in a [[exhibition game|friendly game]] against [[Greece national basketball team|Greece]], Teodosić made a game-winning three-point field goal from about nine meters distance in the quarterfinals, sending Serbia into the semi-finals with a 92–89 upset of [[Spain men's national basketball team|Spain]]. He was also named to the All-Tournament Team. [[File:Miloš Teodosić .jpg|thumb|left|180px|Teodosić with [[Serbia men's national basketball team|Serbia]] in 2011]] He was also a part of the team at the [[EuroBasket 2011]], in Lithuania, which took eighth place. Teodosić was a member of the Serbian roster that won the silver medal at the [[2014 FIBA Basketball World Cup]], under [[head coach]] [[Aleksandar Đorđević]]. He was also named to the All-Tournament Team, as he averaged 13.6 points and 4.4 assists per game, over 9 tournament games.{{cite news|title=Teodosić u idealnom timu, Irving MVP|url=http://www.b92.net/sport/spanija2014/vesti.php?yyyy=2014&mm=09&dd=14&nav_id=899794|access-date=September 15, 2014|work=b92.net|language=sr}}{{cite web|title=Milos TEODOSIC|url=https://www.fiba.basketball/basketballworldcup/2014/player/Milos-Teodosic|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140804005908/http://www.fiba.com/basketballworldcup/2014/Milos-TEODOSIC|url-status=live|archive-date=August 4, 2014|website=fiba.com|access-date=September 15, 2014}} He [[captain (sports)|captained]] the senior Serbia national team for the first time in his career at the [[EuroBasket 2015]].{{cite news|title=AMBITIOUS SERBIA UNVEIL POWERFUL 12-MAN SQUAD|url=http://www.eurobasket2015.org/en/compID_qMRZdYCZI6EoANOrUf9le2.season_2015.roundID_9322.coid_xUMkR0x,HeIT9w-vv9Ob00.articleMode_on.html|access-date=September 3, 2015|work=eurobasket2015.org|date=September 2, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150905064710/http://www.eurobasket2015.org/en/compID_qMRZdYCZI6EoANOrUf9le2.season_2015.roundID_9322.coid_xUMkR0x,HeIT9w-vv9Ob00.articleMode_on.html|archive-date=September 5, 2015|url-status=usurped}} In the first phase of the tournament, Serbia dominated [[EuroBasket 2015 Group B|Group B]], with a 5–0 record, and then eliminated [[Finland national basketball team|Finland]] and the [[Czech Republic national basketball team|Czech Republic]] in the round of 16 and quarterfinal games, respectively.
